newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Leotard calls for reshuffle or election.
newsitem.headline: France's Leotard calls for reshuffle or election.

text.p: A key political partner of France's conservative government on Sunday urged President Jacques Chirac to re-shuffle his cabinet, call an early election or announce a referendum to stem rising popular discontent.
Former defence minister Francois Leotard, head of the UDF junior partner in the ruling coalition, told TF1 television French society had become "wounded, emotional and sceptical".

"I believe this is dangerous and the government had better listen," he said in the interview. He said the constitution gave Chirac three solutions -- dissolve parliament, call a referendum or change the cabinet.
"I hope he will push one of these three buttons...within three or four months," he said.

The popularity of Chirac and Gaullist Prime Minister Alain Juppe has fallen to near-record lows in the face of a stagnating economy, record unemployment and budget austerity imposed to help France meet the criteria to join the single European currency.
The UDF has become increasingly restive recently, criticising Juppe's austerity policies.

The centre-right coalition of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) and the Union for French Democracy (UDF) has an overwhelming majority in parliament. The next general election is scheduled in 1998.
